text:
Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called a "reservoir," which processes input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically not trained; instead, the network learns only the readout weights that map the reservoir's state to the desired output. Training usually involves presenting input data to the reservoir and adjusting the output weights to minimize error.
